_readme: Public DFIR research images we can validate against. Committed so a fresh
session knows what exists without re-researching it, and so 'we tested against
a real device' names WHICH device.
Every entry is a full-filesystem image that ALSO contains an iTunes/Finder
backup. Only the backup half is kept locally: it is what this app reads, it is
~2 GB against ~22 GB for the archive, and disk is the binding constraint (see
scripts/fetch-test-image.sh, which deletes the archive once the backup is out).
SOURCE AND TERMS: Josh Hickman's research images, hosted by Digital Corpora,
which states its images 'are freely available and may be used without prior
`backup_password` is the password Hickman sets on the backup and publishes in
the accompanying documentation. It is not a secret and it protects nothing —
`have` is not recorded here: what is on disk is what is on disk, and a flag in
a committed file would go stale the moment someone prunes. Ask the script.

images.notes: The image every parser and module in the repo is currently validated against. 14,773 manifest entries, 57 third-party apps.

Fetched. `ios`/`device` are read from the fetched backup's Info.plist, not from the upstream description, which says iPhone 12 / 16.5 — what is on disk is an iPhone 11 (serial F4GZ987AN72N) at 16.1.2, the SAME physical device as ios17 one OS earlier. That makes it the ideal drift check: same data, different iOS. The password was recorded as null and is not; it decrypts with the same one as ios17, which is why every module 'failed' against it in corpus mode.
